facts.statement: Tapuiasaurus was named by a research team led by Hussam Zaher in a 2011 publication.
facts.quote: This genus was named a team of researchers led by Hussam Zaher, including Diego Pol, Alberto B. Carvalho, Paulo M. Nascimento aka Pirula (YouTuber), Claudio Riccomini, Peter Larson, Rubén Juárez Valieri, Ricardo Pires Domingues, Nelson Jorge da Silva Jr. and Diógenes de Almeida Campos, in a 2011 publication.

facts.statement: Tapuiasaurus lived during the Aptian age of the Lower Cretaceous in what is now Minas Gerais, Brazil.
facts.quote: Tapuiasaurus (meaning "Tapuia lizard") is a genus of titanosaur which lived during the Lower Cretaceous period (Aptian age) in what is now Minas Gerais, Brazil.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tapuiasaurus were recovered from the Quiricó Formation in the São Francisco Basin of eastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Its fossils, including a partial skeleton with a nearly complete skull, have been recovered from the Quiricó Formation of the São Francisco Basin in Minas Gerais, eastern Brazil.

facts.statement: Later studies suggested Tapuiasaurus has a distant connection to Nemegtosaurus and a close relationship with other Gondwanan lithostrotians.
facts.quote: Wilson et al. (2016) found that Tapuiasaurus falls outside the Lithostrotia shade while Carballido et al. (2017) discovered a close relationship between Tapuiasaurus and the Gondwanan lithostrotians Isisaurus and Rapetosaurus, suggesting a distant connection to Nemegtosaurus.

facts.statement: Tapuiasaurus macedoi is the only known species of this extinct genus, which lived approximately 120 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Middle Cretaceous in South America.
facts.quote: Tapuiasaurus macedoi es la única especie conocida del género extinto Tapuisaurus ("lagarto de Tapuia") de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano, que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente 120 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Tapuiasaurus is known for a nearly complete skull measuring 48 centimeters, and it is believed to have reached a length of 13 meters.
facts.quote: Tapuiasaurus es el noveno titanosaurio encontrado en Brasil. De las 50 especies conocidas, casi todas fueron descritos por un par de costillas o vértebras, Tapuiasaurus es conocido por un cráneo casi completo de 48 centímetros, y se cree que llegó a medir 13 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The teeth of Tapuiasaurus were thin and cylindrical with low cutting edges.
facts.quote: Los dientes son delgados y cilíndricos con bordes cortantes bajos.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found on August 14, 2008, near Coração de Jesus in northern Minas Gerais, Brazil.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MZSP-PV 807, fue encontrado el 14 de agosto de 2008 cerca de Coração de Jesus en el norte del estado de Minas Gerais en las colinas de Embira-Branca en capas de la Formación Quiricó que datan del Aptiense.

facts.statement: The skull is the most complete ever excavated from a titanosaurid, though it is very flattened laterally.
facts.quote: El cráneo es el más completo jamás excavado de un titanosáurido, pero está muy aplanado lateralmente.

facts.statement: The original describers placed Tapuiasaurus within Titanosauria in the clade Lithostrotia as the sister species to Rapetosaurus in Nemegtosauridae.
facts.quote: Según un análisis cladístico exacto realizado por los descriptores, Tapuiasaurus se colocó dentro de Titanosauria en el clado Lithostrotia como la especie hermana de Rapetosaurus en Nemegtosauridae.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis concluded that the previously found close relationship with Rapetosaurus was an artifact caused by the rarity of skulls in Sauropoda.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2016, un análisis concluyó que Tapuiasaurus se inferiría más en Titanosauria y que la relación cercana encontrada previamente con Rapetosaurus es un artefacto de los cráneos de ambas formas, que son raros en Sauropoda.

facts.statement: The time range for Tapuiasaurus is estimated to be between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
